description: KCOV configuration for the A2 control-flow check. Witnesses are not listed here: each mirror decision (leanux-model --decisions) carries source spans for its outcomes, and the check intersects them with the lines that own a KCOV instrumentation point in these functions of the built kernel. 'files' bounds the source considered; 'functions' must include every function whose code (including inlined helpers) the modeled paths execute, and the check fails if coverage lands in a decision span the map does not know. 'known_gaps' lists C choice points KCOV observes but the mirror does not yet model; hits are reported, not failed. 'functions' scopes witnesses: only their PCs witness decisions, and a span line of an anchored C file covered by any other function fails the check; header helpers inlined into unlisted functions are not checked. 'branch_free_functions' lists C functions the compiler made branch-free (no KCOV point); only their decisions may lack an instrumented function. 'shared_exits' declares single instrumentation points, each named by its exact DWARF frame chain (file:line, innermost first; the check requires the chain to name exactly one point of the listed functions), that the compiler shares between a function's early returns and an inlined helper's exit: when the operation did not cover the 'unless_covered' point (the block entering the helper, also exactly one point), the helper's frame there does not count as the helper having run. 'operand_exclusions' declares single call sites of a comparison decision whose operand is a guest-wide value the mirror does not model: the mirror reports the outcome there with 'operands_excluded' instead of the pair, and the check requires Linux's comparison at that call site (outermost frame = 'call'). Both are documented in correspondence/README.md.

shared_exits.note: vfs_write's early returns (-EBADF 668, -EINVAL 670, -EFAULT 672, rw_verify_area's error 676) jump into the epilogue at the KCOV call of file_end_write's not-regular return block (fs.h:3018 inlined at read_write.c:691; return PC 0xffffffff811a279e in the accepted build): the point runs on those paths although file_end_write did not. On the paths that reach file_end_write, the block entering it (read_write.c:691 in vfs_write's own frame, return PC 0xffffffff811a2778) runs first and the early returns skip it, so the declaration applies only when that point is not covered. Found by the generated pipes suite (writes to a read end), deterministic in corpus/pipes/p_wrong_end. vfs_read's counterpart (567) is vfs_read's own frame and needs no declaration; the early returns' false spans leave both points out.

The merged-return-block class (the cookie arms of receive.c:140-164, vfs_write's epilogue above): file_update_time's early return (ret <= 0 at inode.c:2272-2273, the "nothing" outcome) shares its return block with the inlined __file_update_time's (inode.c:2240 inlined at :2275; return PC 0xffffffff811cfd8f in the accepted build), so the point is covered on the nothing path although __file_update_time did not run, and its frame at :2275 witnesses the opposite outcome. On the paths that reach __file_update_time its entering block (file_inode at fs.h:1166 inlined at inode.c:2241, return PC 0xffffffff811cfd6c) runs first and the early return skips it, so the declaration applies only when that point is not covered; then the point neither counts as the helper running nor witnesses a decision outcome. Reached when two writes to a pipe fall in the same 4 ms tick (one coarse clock read, equal stamps): found by the generated pipes suite in the int-r claim point, pipes-20260920-00110 (seed 20260920) operation 16, under eight guests; timing-dependent, not deterministic in any corpus trace.

epoll stream S: ep_insert's and ep_modify's identical tails (`if (pwake) ep_poll_safewake(ep, NULL, 0); return 0;`) are one block in the built code, attributed to ep_modify's return (:1979 under do_epoll_ctl's MOD case :2604), reached at the end of every EPOLL_CTL_ADD. ep_modify's own path runs its smp_mb() block (:1952) first; when that point is not covered, ep_modify did not run.

epoll stream S: do_epoll_wait's `return -EBADF` (:2660) jumps into the epilogue of the error_fput fdput (:2680), whose two points (the FDPUT_FPUT test and the join after it) share this chain; the point of :2674 (`ep = fd_file(f)->private_data`) runs only once the descriptor was found, so when it is not covered fdput did not run (the -EINVAL exit at :2668 runs it, and the mirror reports its decision).

epoll stream S: ep_alloc_epitem's percpu_counter_dec on its -ENOMEM path (:1766) and ep_register_epitem's on its attach-error path (:1808) are one block in the built code, attributed to the latter; the steered epitem failure (e_alloc_epitem_nomem) reaches it without ep_register_epitem running. ep_register_epitem's own path runs its `if (tep)` block (:1800) first. arch/x86/include/asm/irqflags.h is anchored only so this chain can be named.

operand_exclusions.label: __refcount_add.old_zero
operand_exclusions.note: get_current_user() -> get_uid() -> refcount_inc(&root_user.__count) is inlined into alloc_pipe_info (fs/pipe.c:794), so __refcount_add's comparison at refcount.h:189 is recorded there with the guest-wide reference count of root_user (every root credential, kernel threads included; 26 or 27 across runs), which the mirror does not model: the precedent of alloc_empty_file.nr_files_at_max. The outcome (a live root_user: not zero) is reported and A2-checked; only the operands at this call site are excluded. Every other refcount_inc keeps its operands.

operand_exclusions.label: __refcount_add.old_zero
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S: get_current_user() in ep_alloc (fs/eventpoll.c:1343), inlined into do_epoll_create, whose frame at :2412 is the outermost: the same guest-wide root_user count as the fs/pipe.c:794 entry; the outcome (a live root_user) is reported, the operands at this call site excluded.

operand_exclusions.label: do_epoll_ctl.gen_matches
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S (docs/2026-10-12-epoll-design.md 3.5): fs/eventpoll.c's boot-global loop_check_gen, two higher after every full check of every trace of a boot; the mirror's counter is relative to the boot's base (2 after the fixture's warm-up). The outcome at :2552 is checked (false: a fresh set's gen of 0 and a visited set's odd gen never meet the even counter); only the operands are excluded.

operand_exclusions.label: ep_loop_check_proc.visited
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S: the in-check test of a set already visited (a diamond), fs/eventpoll.c:2302; the outcome is checked, the operands are the absolute counter.

operand_exclusions.label: ep_get_upwards_depth_proc.visited
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S: the upward walk's visited test, fs/eventpoll.c:2344 (ep_get_upwards_depth_proc.isra.0's own frame); the outcome is checked, the operands are the absolute counter.

operand_exclusions.label: ep_loop_check_proc.visited
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S: the built code inlines ep_loop_check_proc's recursive call one level, so the inner visit's compare has the recursion site (:2315) as its outermost frame.

operand_exclusions.label: ep_get_upwards_depth_proc.visited
operand_exclusions.note: epoll stream S: as above for ep_get_upwards_depth_proc's recursion site (:2347).
